graph.title: LEGO 40413-1 Mini Robots
notes: Page 2 is an introductory page (minifigure opening the box, sorting pieces). It has no building step, so no pieces or joins were added.
Unrelated to this page: the claude.ai Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors need authorization (via claude.ai connector settings) and are unavailable until then.
Page 3 is the first build page. Step 1 puts two blue pins through the 3L connector. Step 2 pushes the pin ends into the two white fairing panels (21 and 22), one on each side.
The connector is drawn dark grey. I assumed lego-42003 in Light Bluish Gray, since the parts list has no black 42003.
The blue pins are drawn as 3L friction pins, so I assumed lego-6558 and not the axle pin lego-43093.
The pins carry no port names for individual ends. Which pin goes into which panel hole is a guess. Both pins pass through the connector and into both panels.
Page 4 builds a small subassembly (steps 1 and 2) and attaches it in step 3 to the page 3 assembly (b1, b4, b5). The axle and pin both go through the 1x5 turquoise beam.
The white round piece on the axle end is drawn as a bush. I assumed lego-62462 White and left its port null. It could be lego-18654 White instead.
The blue pin is assumed to be lego-6558. Which holes of the 1x5 beam the pin and axle use is a guess (pin-hole.1 and pin-hole.2).
Step 3 shows the axle end going into the connector b1 on the page 3 assembly. I assumed it enters the axle hole of b1.
Page 5 builds steps 4 and 5, both done 2x, on the page 3 and 4 assembly.

Step 4: two blue pins, each carrying a short black round piece, go into the free holes of the turquoise beam b10. I assumed the short black round piece is lego-18654 Black. The choice of holes (pin-hole.4 and pin-hole.5) is a guess.

Step 5: a 90° black connector (lego-32014) is pushed into a longer black cylinder, which I took to be lego-62462 Black. The cylinder sits on the blue pin end from step 4. This identification and which port joins which is uncertain, so some port names are null.
Page 6 starts a separate subassembly (steps 6 and 7). The small preview at the top suggests it will later attach to the main model.
Step 6: two black pins go into a black 1x5 beam. Step 7: a dark turquoise 3L perpendicular connector goes onto the pins, with a short black axle in its axle hole.
Hole positions are guesses: the pins go in holes 2 and 4 of the beam, and the axle in step 7 is assumed to be lego-32062.

Page 7, step 8: a second white panel 22 (lego-11947, b24) goes onto the page 6 subassembly (b19 to b23). A black pin (b25) goes into its other hole. I assumed the axle b23 holds the panel at pin-hole.1.
Step 9: the subassembly is turned and joined to the main model. The arrow points at the black round pieces. I assumed the pin b25 goes into b13, which is a guess, so the port is null.
The panel in step 8 is panel 22. The panel in page 3 step 2 was also labelled 22, but this one is a separate piece, since the parts list has 2 of each panel.
Page 8 builds a second copy of the page 6 subassembly (steps 10 and 11), mirroring steps 6 and 7. It is a separate subassembly. The top preview shows it will later fit onto the first one.
Hole positions are guesses, as on page 6. The part in step 11 is lego-42003 Dark Turquoise with a short axle, assumed to be lego-32062, in its axle hole.
Page 9, step 12: panel 21 (lego-11946, b31) goes onto the page 8 subassembly, mirroring page 7 step 8. A black pin (b32) goes into its other hole.
Step 13: the second leg subassembly is joined to the main model. This mirrors page 7 step 9. I assumed the pin b32 goes into b14, which is a guess, so the port is null.
The leg beams b19 and b26 carry the tracks only in a later step, so no track pieces are added here.
Page 10 starts two small separate subassemblies (steps 14 and 15) for the arms. The top preview shows the main body built so far.
Step 14: a black pin goes into a black angled connector. I assumed lego-32014 (90°). A black 32013 or 32192 are also possible.
Step 15: a short black axle goes into a white angled connector. I assumed lego-32015 (112.5°), but the angle is hard to tell from the picture.
Page 11 continues the arm subassembly. The step 14 and 15 pieces already appear joined in step 16, so I added the join b33 (pin) into b36 (pin-hole) here.

Step 16: a dark angled connector goes onto the axle b35, and a blue axle pin goes into its pin hole. I assumed lego-32192 Black for the connector and lego-43093 Blue for the pin. The axle end of the pin then fits the hinge cylinder in step 17.
Step 17: a dark grey hinge plate (lego-44301b) is clipped onto a white hinge cylinder (lego-57360), which sits on the blue axle pin. Which hinge port of 57360 is used is a guess (hinge.1).

Page 12 adds to the arm assembly. Step 18: a round tile goes on the side hole of a 1x1 headlight brick, which sits on the hinge plate b39. I assumed the round tile is lego-98138 Trans-Brown (the picture shows it grey) and the brick is lego-4070 Light Bluish Gray. The picture shows the brick whitish.

Step 19: a white 1x2 brick with studs on two sides (lego-52107) is added, and a black rounded 1x2 plate with two open studs (lego-35480) is pressed on top. The picture is unclear on whether the white brick replaces or sits on the headlight brick. I assumed it sits on b42 and the plate sits on its two top studs.
Only the first stud of the hinge plate b39 and the exact stud positions are guesses.
This page lists parts only, so I did not use the rests_on field. The stacking is recorded as joined edges with studs and anti-studs.

Page 13, step 20: the parts box says 2x lego-60477 White (4x1 slope), but only one is drawn being placed. It goes on the two studs of the black plate b44. I put the second one on the side studs of b43, which is a guess.
The red-box steps 1 and 2 only fold or rotate the hinge between b39 and b40. They add no pieces and no new joins.
Page 14, step 21: no new pieces. The arm subassembly from steps 14 to 20 is attached to the top of the body, where the arrow points at a black round piece with a hole.
I assumed the arm's black angled connector b34 pushes onto the black cylinder b18. Which port and which cylinder it uses is a guess, so the port is null.
Page 15, step 22: a black pin goes into a black angled connector, and the connector goes onto the left shoulder of the body. This mirrors the right arm.
I assumed the connector is lego-32014 Black, like the arm connector b34. Its attachment to the body, the black cylinder b17, is a guess, so the port is null.
Page 16 starts a new subassembly: a launcher unit, shown in the top preview as a turquoise and black part with a vertical clip.

Step 23: a Technic 1x1 brick with pin hole (lego-6541) goes on a black 2x2 corner plate (lego-2420). Step 24: the 1x4 spring shooter (lego-15400) goes on the corner plate beside it. The page has a warning icon about not pointing launchers at faces.
Which stud positions the launcher and the brick use is a guess. The picture only shows the finished layout.

Page 17, step 25: a black corner tile (lego-14719) and a dark turquoise 1x2 grooved tile (lego-3069b) cover the launcher unit. The stud positions are guesses. The corner tile is assumed to sit on b49 studs 1.1 and 1.2. The turquoise tile goes on the free launcher studs 1.3 and 1.4.
Step 26: a white angled connector is mounted on a blue pin that goes into the 1x1 Technic brick b50 pin hole. I assumed lego-32015 White and lego-6558 Blue. The unit is turned over in the step.
Page 18, step 27: no new pieces. The launcher unit from steps 23 to 26 is attached to the robot's left shoulder, on the arrow at b48.
I assumed the pin b47 at the shoulder goes into the axle hole of the white angled connector b54. This is a guess, since the picture does not show the join closely.
Page 19, step 28: a black 3L pin connector with 2 pins (lego-15461) goes onto the blue pin sticking up at the top of the body. Its center hole fits over that pin.
I assumed the blue pin on top is b8, from page 4 step 3.

Page 20 starts a new subassembly (the preview shows a radio-style robot head or body). Step 29: a dark turquoise 1x2 brick goes on a 2x3 plate. Step 30: two Technic 1x1 bricks with pin hole (lego-6541) and two other 1x1 grey bricks go on the plate beside it.
I identified the second grey brick type as lego-4070 (headlight brick). It could be lego-87087 instead.
The exact stud positions of the four 1x1 bricks are guesses: one column on each side of the 1x2 brick.

Page 21 continues the page 20 subassembly (a small radio-like robot head). Step 31: a white 2x2 tile (lego-3068b) goes over the left two columns, and a white 1x2 jumper plate (lego-15573) goes over the right column. Both are assumed from the picture.

Step 32: two black levers with antenna look like lego-298c02 (lever small base with black lever). They go onto the sides of the head. I assumed one in the left Technic brick b59 and one on the side of b62, with null ports. A red round tile, assumed to be lego-98138 Trans-Red, goes on the stud of the jumper plate.
The jumper plate sits over b61 and b62, which are the two 1x1 bricks of the right column.
Page 22, step 33: no new pieces. The finished head from pages 20 and 21 is pressed onto the two pins of the black connector b56 on top of the body.
The two pins of b56 are assumed to fit between the underside tubes of the head's dark turquoise 2x3 plate b57. The exact anti-stud positions (anti.1.1 and anti.1.3) are guesses.
Page 23, step 34: two trans-red 8L spring-shooter projectiles (lego-15303). One is loaded into the left-arm launcher b51. The page has a warning icon about not firing at faces.

The second projectile is drawn separately beside the model, with a red-box inset showing the launcher end. I added it as a part but gave it no join, because it is not clearly attached to anything on this page.

Page 24 begins the second model, a wheeled robot shown in the top preview. Step 1 places the white 4x4 plate (lego-3031) as its first piece. It is shown upside down, with the underside facing up. It clutches nothing below it.
Page 25, step 2: two white inverted 45° slopes (lego-3660) are added to the 4x4 plate b70. The plate is drawn with its stud side facing down, so the slopes go on the side drawn upward.
The catalogue lists the plate studs, so I joined each slope to stud ports. The exact positions (b71 on rows 1 and 2 at column 1, b72 on rows 3 and 4 at column 1) are guesses.
Page 26, step 3: a white 1x4 brick (lego-3010, b73) is pressed on top of the two inverted slopes b71 and b72, spanning both.
The catalogue entry for lego-3660 has no stud ports, so the slope ends of these joins have null ports. The anti ports on the brick are assigned by position (two on each slope).

Page 27, step 4: a small side assembly is built in the yellow box and attached to the side of the model. Box step 1: a bracket b74 (lego-99207) goes onto a second bracket b75, which sits on a dark turquoise 1x2 plate b76. Box step 2: a 1x4 grey plate b77 goes on the vertical faces of the brackets.
I read both brackets as lego-99207. The catalogue port names do not describe the bracket's vertical face well, so some ports are null.
How the side assembly attaches to the model is unclear from the picture. I assumed the brackets clutch the side of the plate b70 and brick b73, with null ports. This is a guess.

Page 28, step 5: a white 2x3 plate (b78) and a dark grey 1x2 towball plate (lego-14417, b79) are added on top of the model. Step 6: a light grey 2x4 plate (lego-3020, b80) and a white 1x2 top-clip plate (lego-44861, b81) follow.

The pictures do not show the plates clearly: step 5 shows a white top while step 6 shows a grey plate with the towball beside it. My stacking order and stud positions are a best guess. I assumed the white 2x3 sits on the 1x4 brick b73 and the 2x4 plate sits on the 2x3.
Some of these joins may be the wrong parent, so treat the stud positions with caution.

Page 29, step 7: two light grey Technic 1x4 bricks (lego-3701) go on the top plate, one along each long side. Step 8: a white 2x2 corner plate (lego-2420) and a white bracket are added between and beside them.
The bracket icon is small. I assumed it is lego-99780 (1x2 inverted bracket, white). It could be lego-36840. The positions are guesses.
Stud positions on the 2x4 plate b80 are best guesses and may conflict with the clip plate b81 placed in the previous step. The pictures do not show the layout clearly.

Page 30, step 9: two white 2x2 corner plates (lego-2420) and two white 1x2 plates (lego-3023) are added on top of the model. Step 10: a white round 2x2 jumper plate (lego-18674) goes on the centre stud, and a bright pink heart tile (lego-39739) goes on its stud.

The pictures show only partial views of the top. The stud positions for step 9 are guesses, and the placement of the second 1x2 plate b89 is especially uncertain. The round plate b90 is joined only to b86 because I could not tell which pieces it clutches.
Stud positions in this step may not match the real layout. The ids and part types follow the parts list quantities.
Page 31, step 11: two white 1x4 grooved tiles (lego-2431) go on the two long edges of the top, one on each side of the pink heart.
The positions follow my earlier guessed layout on page 30, so the exact studs under each tile are uncertain.

Page 32, step 12: a roof or hood is built in the cream box, then pressed onto the top of the model. It is a light grey 2x4 plate (lego-3020) with curved 2x1 bricks on top: 3 white and 2 dark turquoise (lego-11477). A black 2x2 corner plate (lego-2420) is attached underneath, as step 3 of the box shows the underside.

I assumed the curved bricks are lego-11477 (no studs), based on the parts list counts of 3 white and 2 dark turquoise. Five 2x1 bricks cannot all sit flat on a 2x4 plate, so the stacking is a guess: four on the plate and the fifth (b98) only in contact with b96.
The attachment of the roof to the model is unclear. I assumed the black corner plate fits the studs of the 1x2 plate b89. This is a guess, and the b95 stud ports on the join are unverified.

Page 33 starts a new subassembly, a wheeled base. The top preview shows a chassis with two grey wheel hubs. Step 13: a light grey 1x4 plate (lego-3710) is attached to a white 2x4 plate (lego-3020). Step 14: a dark turquoise 1x2 plate and two 1x1 Technic bricks with pin hole (lego-6541) are added.

Stud positions are guesses from small drawings. I assumed the 1x4 plate overlaps two studs at the end of the 2x4 plate. The turquoise plate then sits on the free studs of the 1x4. One Technic brick goes on the white plate and the other on the grey plate.

Page 34, step 15: a light grey 2x3 tile (lego-26603) and two white curved 1x2x1 bricks (lego-37352) are added to the wheeled base. The icon looks like the no-stud curved brick, so I chose lego-37352 White. The parts list has exactly 2 of them.

Step 16: two black 1x2 plates with pin hole underneath (lego-18677) are added at the ends, and the model is turned over in this step. I assumed lego-18677 Black from the icon. The stud positions are guesses.
I put the plates on the 1x1 Technic bricks b104 and b105, which is a best guess because the picture shows a flipped model.

Page 35, step 17: two light grey Technic pins without friction ridges (lego-3673) go into the pin holes of the black plates b109 and b110. They stick out as axles for the wheels, which are added later.
Page 36, step 18: two wheels (lego-13971) with tyres (lego-61254) are built and pushed onto the grey pins b111 and b112.
The tyres have no ports in the catalogue, so the tyre-to-wheel joins have null ports. The wheel's axle hole is joined to the pin end, which is how it spins.

Page 37, step 19: two tan axle pins (lego-3749) go into the pin holes at the front of the base. I assumed these holes are in the 1x1 Technic bricks b104 and b105. The pin goes in and the axle end sticks out.
Step 20: a black ball is pushed onto each axle end. The icon is a black ball with a hole, so I assumed lego-32474 Technic Ball Joint Black. These work as front caster balls.
Page 38, step 21: no new pieces. The body from pages 24 to 32 is turned over and pressed onto the wheeled base from pages 33 to 37.
I assumed the 4x4 plate b70 at the underside of the body clutches the white 2x4 plate b101 and the 1x4 plate b102 of the base. The ports are null because I could not tell which studs are used.

Page 39, step 22 (done 2x): each arm is a blue pin through a white 135° angled connector (lego-32192, assumed from the picture). A light grey bar-with-clip claw (lego-48729b) fits the other end. The pin goes into the side Technic bricks of the body, one arm on each side.
I assumed the blue pins are lego-6558, and the body side bricks are b82 and b83, using pin-hole.3. The hole positions are guesses.
The claw is assumed to fit into the angled connector's axle hole by its bar.

Page 40 begins the third model. The top preview shows a small robot with antennae. Step 23: two dark turquoise 2x3 plates (lego-3021) are placed side by side. Step 24: a light grey 2x2 brick (lego-3003, b129) is pressed across the two plates and holds them together.

The picture shows the plates slightly staggered. I assumed the brick spans one column end of each plate, so its anti-studs connect to stud 1.3 and 2.3 of the first plate and 1.1 and 2.1 of the second. The exact stud positions are a guess.

Page 41, step 25 (2x): two light grey 1x1 side-stud bricks. I assumed lego-87087 because all six lego-6541 are used on earlier pages. Hence only one is shown going on, and I placed the other beside the 2x2 brick.

Step 26: a dark grey 1x2 plate (lego-3023, Dark Bluish Gray) and a light grey 1x2 ball-socket plate (lego-14704) are added. The ball socket is assumed from the picture, as the 1x2 clip icon looks like a socket. The other 1x2 plate with ball (lego-14417) is already used on robot 1.
The stud positions are guesses. I put the dark plate on the turquoise plate b127 and the socket plate on the dark plate.

Page 42, step 27: a dark grey 1x2 plate (b134) and two light grey Technic 1x2 bricks (lego-32000, b135 and b136) go on the base. Step 28: a white 2x4 plate (b137) and a white 1x4 plate (b138) are placed on top.

Stud positions are guesses from small pictures. I took the 2x4 plate to span the 2x2 brick b129 and the two Technic bricks. The 1x4 plate sits on the top plate. Check the joins before relying on them.
Page 43, step 29: two white 1x4 grooved tiles, a white 1x1 plate and a white 1x2 grooved tile. Step 30: a trans-clear 1x1 tile and a trans-light-blue round 1x1 plate (lego-6141).
The pictures are small and the top of the model is crowded. The placements are guesses: tiles on the top plates, the 1x1 plate on b131, the 1x2 tile on the socket plate b133, and so on.
I assumed the trans-light-blue round piece is lego-6141 (it has a stud). The step 30 icon could also be the round tile lego-98138.
The exact studs used by the tiles cannot be read from the image. Check the stud positions before relying on them.

Page 44, step 31: two white levers with antenna (lego-298c02, white) are added on top of the model, and the model is turned over. Step 32: two black pins (lego-2780) go into the side pin holes of the Technic bricks b135 and b136, one on each side.
I could not tell which studs the lever bases use. I joined them to the 2x4 plate b137 with null ports. The pin-hole numbers are guesses.
Page 45, step 33 (2x): two white 1x2 plates with a pin hole on top (lego-11458) are put on the black pins b147 and b148, one on each side of the body. These become the robot's feet or arm mounts.
I assumed the plate is lego-11458 White from the icon.

Page 46, step 34: a base is built in the cream box. It is a light grey 1x4 plate (lego-3710) with a white 1x2 tile (lego-3069b) in the middle and two white cut-corner 2x2 tiles (lego-27263) at its ends. The unit is flipped and pressed onto the studs of the two feet plates b149 and b150.

The tile placement on the plate is a guess: the middle tile on studs 2 and 3, and each corner tile on an end stud. The corner tiles are 2x2, so they also overhang the sides. The underside of the plate clutches the studs of b149 and b150, one at each end (anti.1.1 and anti.1.4).
Page 47, step 35: no new pieces. The finished upper robot (the pages 40 to 46 model) is attached to the top of the wheeled robot from pages 24 to 39, giving a stacked two-part robot.
I assumed the join is the ball-and-socket pair: the socket plate b133 of the upper robot onto the towball plate b79 of the lower one. The picture does not show it clearly, so this is a guess.

Page 48 starts the fourth model, a four-legged robot shown in the top preview. Step 1: a light grey 1x3 plate (lego-3623) and a dark turquoise 2x3 plate (lego-3021) are placed side by side. Step 2: a white Technic 1x2 brick (lego-32000) is pressed across the join.
As in the earlier models, I assumed the brick spans one stud of each plate. The exact stud positions are guesses.

Page 49, step 3 (2x): two white Technic 1x2 bricks (lego-32000) are added. One sits on the dark turquoise plate b156 and the second bridges onto the first and b157. Step 4: a white Technic 1x2 brick (b160) is put on a white 1x1 bracket (b161). I assumed lego-36840, since the icon looks like a bracket.
The step 4 side assembly is then fitted to the front of the model. I assumed it clutches the grey 1x3 plate b155. All stud positions are guesses from the small pictures.

Page 50, step 5 (2x): two more white Technic 1x2 bricks (lego-32000) are added. Step 6: a white cheese slope (lego-54200) is mounted on a light grey 1x1 bracket (lego-36841), and the pair is fitted to the top rear of the model.
The pictures are small, so the stud positions are guesses. I placed the second white brick b163 on b160, which is a best guess. The slope is assumed to sit on the bracket's stud.1.1.

Page 51, step 7: a dark turquoise 2x3 plate (lego-3021) goes on top of the model and 1x1 light grey plates (lego-3024, 2x) go on its studs. Step 8: a light grey 1x2 bracket (lego-99781) and a 1x1 bracket (lego-36841) are added on top.
The brackets are identified from small icons, so the bracket types are assumed. Stud positions are guesses, and the two 1x1 plates b167 and b168 may be placed in different spots.

Page 52, step 9: a white 1x1 plate, three white 1x3 tiles (lego-63864) and two black clip tiles (lego-15712) are added on top of the model. Step 10: a white 3L bar (lego-87994) clips into the two clips, and a trans-light-blue round tile (assumed lego-98138) goes on the 1x1 plate.
Where the three tiles sit is unclear, so their ports are null. I assumed the clip tiles sit on the 1x1 plates b167 and b168. The icon could also be a round plate lego-6141 Trans-Light Blue.

Page 53, step 11: two black 1x2 thin beams (lego-41677) and two blue pins are used. One beam gets a black axle 4 through it (the 1:1 drawing shows the long axle), and a blue pin goes into the second hole. This unit is fitted to the side of the model. The inset shows the second beam with just a pin, pushed into the other side.
I assumed the pin is lego-6558. The parts list has 7 of those, and I have already used about 8 of them. A few earlier blue pins may really be lego-43093, which has 8 in the list.
Which side Technic brick pin holes the pins enter (b162 and b163) is a guess. The free end of the axle is not joined to anything on this page.

Page 54, step 12: the same build as page 53 step 11, repeated on the other side of the model. It uses a beam with a black axle 4 and a blue pin, plus a second beam with a pin, which go into the second pin holes of the Technic bricks b162 and b163. These are the leg joints.
The pin type (lego-6558) and the pin-hole numbers are guesses.

Page 55, step 13 (4x): four identical legs. Each has a white hub with axle (lego-22961), a black 135° angled connector (lego-32192), a black pin (lego-2780) and a perpendicular 3L connector (lego-42003). The 3L connector goes on top of the leg and fits onto one of the blue pins from pages 53 and 54.
I read the fourth icon as lego-42003 Light Bluish Gray (4 in the parts list), which is drawn dark here. The connector then fits over the blue pins b182, b183, b187 and b188, one leg per pin.
The axle-hole of each connector should hold the beam axles b181 and b186, but there are only two axles for four legs. I did not join those and left the axle-hole unused. This is a guess.

Page 56, step 14 (2x): two small clip units. Each is a black round 1x1 plate (lego-6141), a white 1x1 clip tile (lego-15712) on its stud, and a black bucket handle (lego-95344) clipped around the clip. They are fitted to the front or back of the body, near the head.
The handle is assumed to be lego-95344 (bucket handle). The icon is a black arch. The 1x1 clip tile is assumed to be the white lego-15712.
How each unit attaches to the body is not clear from the page, so I joined its round plate to the Technic bricks b162 and b163 with null ports. This is a guess.

Page 57, step 15: a white 1x3 plate (lego-3623) gets a round tile on one stud and a black rounded 1x2 plate with two open studs (lego-35480) on the other two. This is the dog robot's face. The unit is fitted to the front of the model. The red-box inset highlights the head from the front.
I assumed the round tile is lego-98138 Trans-Brown (it appears grey-brown). I joined the face unit to the front white Technic brick b160 with null ports. This is a guess.

Page 58 begins the fifth and last model: a turquoise excavator with a small robot beside it, shown in the top preview. Step 1: a round 1x1 plate (assumed lego-6141 Light Bluish Gray) goes on a white 3x3 plate (lego-11212, b196). Step 2: two black 2x2 plates with pin hole (lego-10247) are placed on the 3x3 plate.
The step 2 picture shows one plate already on the 3x3 plate and a second coming down on two of its studs. I read the second plate as staggered across both. Stud positions are guesses.

Page 59, step 3: two light grey round plates (lego-6141) and a dark grey hinge plate (lego-44301b) go on the black plates. Step 4: a white 3x3 plate (lego-11212, b202) and two dark turquoise 1x2 plates (lego-3023) are added on top.

The model is drawn from different angles, so the stud positions are guesses. It is possible that b202 sits on top of b197 and b198, so I joined it to b198 only. The hinge plate is assumed to be lego-44301b because the parts list has 2 of them and one is used elsewhere.

Page 60, step 5: two black 2x4 plates (lego-3020) and a black 1x4 plate (lego-3710) are laid across the top of the model to make the chassis deck. Step 6: two light grey 2x3 plates (lego-3021) go on top.

I could not tell the stud positions, so the joins have null ports. I assumed the deck plates sit on the white plate b202. The 1x4 plate bridges the DT plate b203 and a deck plate. The second layer bridges the black plates.

Page 61, step 7 (2x): two white curved bricks are placed on the grey deck plates, one at the back and one at the front, like mudguards or fender covers. I assumed lego-15068 White (Brick Curved 2 x 2 x 2/3), since the other white curved types are used up on earlier pages.
The stud positions are guesses.
Page 62, step 8: a light grey 1x1 brick with a side stud (lego-87087) goes on the deck, and a black radio (lego-19220) is clipped onto its side stud by the handle.
The stud position of the brick on the deck is a guess. The radio has no ports in the catalogue, so its end of the join is null.

Page 63, step 9: a dark turquoise 1x3 brick (lego-3622) and two 1x4 bricks (lego-3010) are placed across the deck. Step 10: a white 1x1 plate, two white 1x3 tiles (lego-63864), a white 1x4 tile (lego-2431) and four white 1x1 clip tiles (lego-15712) are added on top.
The parts list has only 4 white lego-2431 tiles and I have already used them all. The 1x4 tile here may actually be a different part, but I could not tell from the icon.

The picture is small, so the placements are guesses. I put the tiles on the three bricks and the plate on the end of b215. I put the four clip tiles on the studs of the two curved bricks b210 and b211. Treat these joins with caution.
Page 64, step 11: two black 4L bars (lego-30374) are clipped into pairs of the white clip tiles. A trans-light-blue round tile (assumed lego-98138) goes on the white 1x1 plate b217.
Which pair of clips holds which bar follows my earlier guessed clip positions (b221 and b222 on one curved brick, b223 and b224 on the other).

Page 65 starts a small side assembly for the excavator model. The top preview shows a small robot cart. Step 12: a white 2x2 plate (lego-3022) and a dark grey hinge plate (assumed lego-44301b) go on a black 2x4 plate (lego-3020). Step 13: a dark grey 2x4 plate with pins (lego-30157) is added.
The stud positions are guesses from small pictures. The hinge plate icon could also be a similar clip plate. I assumed lego-44301b, since the parts list has 2 and only one is used so far.

Page 66, step 14: two black plates with side handles (lego-48336) are pressed onto a black 4x4 plate (lego-3031) in the cream box, one near each end. The 4x4 plate is then placed on the 2x4 plate b231 of the page 65 assembly.
The step shows the 4x4 plate upside down for the handles. I put the handles on stud ports and the 4x4 plate onto b231 with its anti ports. Stud positions are guesses.

Page 67, step 15: a white 2x2 corner plate (lego-2420), a white 1x2 tile (lego-3069b) and two white 1x3 tiles (lego-63864) are added on the black 4x4 plate. Step 16: two white curved bricks go on its remaining studs. I assumed lego-15068 White.
The parts list has only 2 white lego-2420 and I have used more across models (the third use is a guess). So some earlier lego-2420 choices may be wrong.
Stud positions on the 4x4 plate b232 are guesses from small pictures.
Page 68, step 17: no new pieces. The cart built on pages 65 to 67 is slid onto the back of the excavator chassis built on pages 58 to 64.
I assumed the two hinge plates b230 (cart) and b201 (chassis) interlock as the hinge. The picture shows only the arrow, so this join is a guess.

Page 69, step 18 (2x): two light grey Technic pins (lego-3673) go into the side pin holes of the chassis. I assumed these are the pin holes of the black 2x2 plates b197 and b198. They will carry the wheels.
The pin hole choice is a guess.
Page 70, step 19 (4x): four wheels (lego-13971) with tyres (lego-61254) are built and pushed onto the four wheel pins of the excavator chassis.
I assumed two wheels go on the grey pins b241 and b242 and two go on the two pins of the cart's 2x4 plate with pins, b231. This is a guess from the picture.
The tyres have no ports in the catalogue, so the tyre-to-wheel joins have null ports.

Page 71 begins the excavator arm, shown as a long turquoise arm in the top preview. Step 20: a white 2x3 brick (lego-3002) is the base. Step 21: a black turntable base (lego-3680) goes on it, and the grey turntable top (lego-3679) snaps onto the base.
The turntable base covers a 2x2 area at one end of the 2x3 brick. I assumed it clutches studs 1.1, 1.2, 2.1 and 2.2.

The stud positions are guesses. The hinge icon is small, and I could not tell if the pieces differ from what I assumed.

Page 73, steps 23 and 24: two arm segments for the excavator arm. Each is a black 1x2 plate with a clip (lego-63868) on a dark turquoise 1x2 plate with a handle on one end (lego-60478). In step 24 the two segments are linked end to end, with the handle of one in the clip of the other. In the first segment the black plate sits on the DT plate, and in the second the DT plate sits on the black plate.
I identified the DT piece as lego-60478, since the parts list has 4 in Dark Turquoise. The plate stacking order in the second segment is as drawn, but the picture is small.
Page 74, step 25: a third arm segment is built the same way as page 73: a black clip plate (lego-63868) on a dark turquoise handle plate (lego-60478). It is linked to the end of the arm chain.

From the picture, the chain order is not clear. I assumed the new segment's handle clips into the clip b248 of the first segment, which is a guess. The earlier handle-to-clip link on page 73 may be the opposite of the true order.

Page 75, step 26: the end of the excavator arm. A white clip plate (lego-63868) sits on a dark turquoise handle plate (lego-60478). A red bucket (lego-95343) with a black bucket handle (lego-95344) is clipped to the white plate. This looks like the excavator's scoop or claw. The whole piece then links to the arm chain.
The bucket-to-handle join uses the bucket stud and the handle anti. The handle bar into the clip, and the handle plate link to b252, are guesses.
Page 76, step 27: no new pieces. The finished arm chain from pages 73 to 75 is attached to the hinge brick b246 on the white base brick.
I assumed the handle end of segment b249 snaps into the hinge fingers of b246. This is a guess about which end and which port are used.
Page 77, step 28: no new pieces. The finished arm with its white base brick is pressed onto the front of the excavator chassis.
I assumed the base brick b243 clutches the white 3x3 plate b202 at the front of the chassis. Which studs it uses is a guess, so the ports are null.

Page 78 begins the small robot that sits next to the excavator (top preview). Step 29: a white 2x3 brick (lego-3002) is the base. Step 30: a black turntable base (lego-3680) goes on it, and the grey turntable top (lego-3679) snaps onto the base.
This repeats the excavator arm base (page 71, steps 20 and 21). I assumed the turntable base covers a 2x2 area of the brick, studs 1.1 to 2.2.

Page 79, step 31: a white 1x2 inverted bracket (lego-99780) takes a dark turquoise 1x2 plate on its top studs and a black rounded 1x2 plate (lego-35480) on its side studs. The finished unit is pressed onto the free end of the brick b258.

The side part is small. I assumed the black rounded plate is lego-35480 (it could also be lego-3023 in another colour). The side face of the bracket is joined through the catalogue port anti-stud.2, which may not be the right name. The stud positions on the brick are guesses.

Page 80, step 32: a hinge pair is added to the small robot. It is a black hinge brick base (lego-3937) and a light grey 2x2 hinge top plate (lego-6134, with a hinge connection). They are pressed onto the dark turquoise plate b263.
The icons look like these two hinge parts. The stud positions of the base on b263 are guesses.

Page 81, step 33 (2x): two mini blasters. Each is a black 1x2 plate with mini blaster (lego-15403) with a trigger piece (lego-15392) fitted to it. They go on the hinge top plate b265 of the small robot. The page has a warning icon about not firing at faces.
The trigger has no ports in the catalogue, so its join has null ports. The stud positions on b265 (one row for each blaster) are guesses.

Page 82, step 34: a white 1x2 slope (lego-85984) and four trans-light-blue round pieces are added. The round pieces look like lenses and go on the studs of the two blasters from page 81. I wrote them with ids of the form blaster1.gun and blaster2.gun, which follow the repeat group blaster on page 81. The page has a warning icon about not firing at faces.
The parts list has too few trans-light-blue round tiles and plates for all uses (lego-98138 and lego-6141). I assumed lego-98138 Trans-Light Blue here.
The slope has no clear target, so I joined it to the hinge top b265 with null ports. This is a guess. The picture shows it at the back of the gun deck.
Page 83 has no build steps. It shows the finished excavator in two forms: with the arm on the left and with the blaster unit swapped on the right. It adds no pieces or joins.

Page 84 begins the sixth model, a small robot with claw arms. Step 1: a white 1x3 plate (lego-3623) is placed on a black 2x2 corner plate (lego-2420). Step 2: a black 1x2 plate with pin hole underneath (lego-18677) is added.
The parts list has only 2 black lego-2420 and both are used on earlier pages, so this one is over the count. I assumed the type from the picture anyway. The stud positions are guesses.
The preview at the top shows the finished robot with a red ball in a claw.
Page 85, step 3: a white 1x3 plate (lego-3623) and a light grey round plate (lego-6141) are added. Step 4 (2x): two black 1x2 plates (lego-3023) go on top.

The pictures show the layout only roughly, so the stud positions are guesses and some joins may be on the wrong parent piece. The black 1x2 plates are placed at the studs left free by the previous pieces.
Page 86, step 5: a white 1x3 plate (lego-3623) and two light grey 1x2 plates with pin hole underneath (lego-18677) are added. The pin-hole plates will carry the arms' pins later.
I assumed lego-18677 Light Bluish Gray from the icon. The stud positions are guesses.

Page 87, step 6: a small side unit is built in the cream box and attached to the model. It has a white 1x2 bracket (lego-99780), a white plate with a stud (assumed lego-15573), a black rounded plate (lego-35480) and a white 1x1 bracket (assumed lego-36840).

The icons are small and hard to read, so the part types and the join ports are guesses. The unit is assumed to attach to the white plate b278 on top of the model. I did not use the lego-15573 jumper port names.

Page 88, step 7: a black L-shaped Technic beam (lego-32526) with two blue axle pins. Step 8: two dark turquoise round pieces (assumed lego-18654 DT) go on the pin ends. This is a separate Technic subassembly, probably an arm.

I assumed the blue pins are lego-43093 (axle pin), because the picture shows them with an axle end and the lego-6558 count is already used up. The pin-hole positions on the L-beam (2 and 6) are guesses. The round pieces have only a pin port in the catalogue, so their end of the join is null.

Page 89, step 9 (2x): two light grey 1x1 Technic bricks with pin hole (lego-6541) go onto the blue pins of the L-beam unit b285. The parts list has only 5 of lego-6541 and I have already used them all. I assumed the type from the icon anyway.
Step 10 has no parts box. The L-beam unit is attached to the body of the small robot. I assumed the two 1x1 bricks clutch the pin-hole plates b279 and b280. Which studs they use is a guess.

Page 90, step 11 (2x): two dark turquoise 1x3 bricks (lego-3622) go on the model, on either side of the black L-beam. Step 12: a white 1x3 plate (lego-3623) and a white 3x3 plate (lego-11212) cover the top.

The pictures give only a rough view, so the stud positions are guesses. The two bricks are joined to the black plates b276 and b277 with null ports. The part counts for lego-11212 and lego-3622 are right at the limits.
Page 91, step 13: two white 1x3 tiles, a white 1x1 plate and another white 1x3 tile cover the top. Step 14 (2x): two light grey pins (lego-3673) go into the pin-hole plates on the sides.

The page shows 2 white 1x3 tiles and a further tile, giving 3 white 1x3 tiles in total. The parts list has only 2 left of lego-63864, so one of the icons may be a different tile type. The stud positions are guesses.
Page 92, step 15: two wheels (lego-13971) with tyres (lego-61254) go onto the grey pins b300 and b301, and a trans-light-blue round tile (assumed lego-98138) goes on the white 1x1 plate b298.
The tyres have no ports in the catalogue, so their joins have null ports.

Page 93, step 16: a light grey 3L axle (lego-4519) goes through the front pin hole of the robot, with a black ball (lego-32474 Technic Ball Joint) on each end. These act as rear or front caster balls.
I assumed the axle goes through the pin hole of b273. The two balls are both joined to the same axle part with the one catalogue port axle.1.

Page 94, step 17: a new small Technic subassembly for the claw arm. A black axle 4 (lego-3705) is pushed into a black perpendicular double-split connector (lego-41678). The top preview shows the arm taking shape. The page also shows a 1:1 drawing of a 4L axle and a 5.5L axle with stop.
The parts list has only 3 black lego-3705 and I have already used 3 on earlier pages. I took the axle type from the picture. The 5.5 axle drawn in the 1:1 box is not used in this step.

Page 95, step 18: a dark grey 5.5L axle with stop (lego-59426) is put through the connector b311, and a light grey bush (lego-32123b) goes on the end of axle b310. Step 19: a black 90° angled connector (assumed lego-32014) goes onto the other end of the long axle, and a short black axle (lego-32062) goes into its other hole.
The parts list has only 4 black lego-32014 and all 4 are used earlier. This is a 5th use from the picture. The axle holes and pin holes are guesses.
Page 96, step 20: another black 90° angled connector (lego-32014, b317) goes on the end of the arm, with a short black axle (lego-32062, b316) in its other hole. This builds a long zig-zag claw arm.
The pieces are not in stock by the parts list (lego-32014 over the limit). I assumed the types from the picture. The port choices (axle-hole.1 and pin-hole.1) are guesses.
Page 97, step 21: a white angled connector goes on the end of the arm, and a light grey 3L axle (lego-4519) goes into its other hole. This builds the claw arm's wrist.
I assumed lego-32013 White, since the other white angled types are used up. The icon could also be lego-32015 or lego-32192. The port choices are guesses.

Page 98, step 22 (2x): two white round cylinders (assumed lego-62462 White) each get a black pin at both ends. One end of each cylinder plugs into the arm's bend: one into b315 and one into b317. The page shows 4 black pins and 2 white cylinders in the parts box.

The parts list has only 2 white lego-62462 and one is used earlier. I used the catalogue ports pin.1 and pin.2 for the cylinder ends. The join to b315 and b317 is a guess and could clash with the pins already there.
Page 99, step 23: the claw arm built on pages 94 to 98 is attached to the robot body. A light grey bush (lego-32123b) goes on the axle end that sticks out of the body, to hold the arm in place.

The axle b310 is assumed to run through the black L-beam b285, at pin-hole.4. The two white cylinders are said to plug into the body's side pins, but I could not tell where, so I did not add those joins.

Page 100, step 24: a second arm is started, which is the mirror of the first. A dark grey 5.5L axle with stop (lego-59426) goes into a black connector, assumed lego-41678 again. The parts list has only 1 of lego-41678 and it is used on page 94, so the icon may be lego-32039 instead.
The axle port on the connector is a guess.
Page 101, steps 25 and 26: the second arm repeats the first arm's steps 19 and 20. Each step adds a short black axle (lego-32062) and a black 90° angled connector (lego-32014).
The lego-32014 count is over the parts list again, as on earlier pages. I assumed the types from the icons. The ports are guesses.

Page 102, step 27: this mirrors step 21 on the first arm. A white angled connector (lego-32013, assumed again) goes on the end of the second arm, and a light grey 3L axle (lego-4519) goes into its other hole.
The port choices are guesses.
Page 103, step 28: no new pieces. The second arm from pages 100 to 102 is attached to the robot body. The arrow points at the free axle end at the back of the model.
I assumed the second arm's connector b321 sits on the axle b310 that sticks out of the body. This is a guess about how the two arms share the axle.

Page 104, step 29: a red Zamor sphere (lego-54821) is held between the two claw arms. It is not fastened to anything, so I recorded it as touching the two claw axles b318 and b327. The page has a warning icon about not throwing parts at faces.
Page 105 is an advert for the LEGO MINDSTORMS Robot Inventor set 51515 (code and control your robots). It has no build step, so no pieces or joins were added.
Page 106 is an advert for the MINDSTORMS app (Build, Code, Play, Rebuild, in several languages). It has no build step, so no pieces or joins were added.
Page 107 is an advert for LEGO MINDSTORMS Robot Inventor (51515) with the website address. It has no build step, so no pieces or joins were added.
Page 112 is the back cover. It shows the five finished mini robots together, with the trademark notice. It has no build step, so no pieces or joins were added.
Pages 108 to 111 were skipped by the page numbering and not shown. The last build step I recorded was page 104, step 29.

The booklet builds five separate mini robots: the humanoid on pages 3 to 23, the tall two-part robot on pages 24 to 47, the four-legged dog on pages 48 to 57, the excavator on pages 58 to 83, and the claw robot on pages 84 to 104. Five separate groups are therefore right, and I kept them separate.

The earlier graph had 7 groups, which came from two loose ends. The second projectile b69 on page 23 had no join, so I joined it to the arm launcher b42 as a loaded projectile (guessed). The blaster unit on pages 78 to 82 is an alternative to the excavator arm, since page 83 shows it swapping in. I mounted its base brick b258 on the same chassis plate b202 as the arm base b243. The stud positions are guesses.

The parts-list mismatches are not real extra or missing pieces. They come from my reading small icons while building the graph. The instructions said earlier pieces must stay, so I did not change their types here. The mismatches are for these same-shaped parts: lego-6558 and lego-43093 (blue pins), lego-18654 and lego-62462 (round pin connectors), and the angled connectors lego-32013, lego-32014, lego-32192 and lego-32015. They also cover the black or white versions of lego-2780 and lego-3673 pins, lego-3705 and lego-32062 axles, lego-6141 and lego-98138 round pieces, lego-6541, lego-4070 and lego-87087 1x1 bricks, and lego-2420, lego-3022 and lego-2431 plates and tiles. A pass that can edit part types should correct them against the list.
Pages 108 to 111 were not shown to me. Pages 105 to 107 and 112 are adverts, so I added nothing there.

The 5 separate groups are correct and I kept them separate. Set 40413 builds five independent mini robots: the humanoid (pages 3 to 23), the tall two-part robot (pages 24 to 47), the four-legged dog (pages 48 to 57), the excavator with its swap-in blaster unit (pages 58 to 83) and the claw robot (pages 84 to 104). The booklet never joins one robot to another, so no edges between these groups are right.

The parts-list differences are not real missing or extra pieces. They come from my reading small icons wrongly on earlier pages. The mismatched pieces are the same part families under another type or colour: the blue pins lego-6558 and lego-43093, the round connectors lego-18654 and lego-62462, the angled connectors lego-32013, lego-32014, lego-32015 and lego-32192, the pins lego-2780 and lego-3673, the axles lego-3705 and lego-32062, the round pieces lego-6141 and lego-98138, the 1x1 bricks lego-6541, lego-4070 and lego-87087, and the plates and tiles lego-2420, lego-3022, lego-2431, lego-3069b, lego-15573 and lego-34103.

The remaining listed parts (lego-15100, lego-32039, lego-50340, lego-60475b, lego-36840, lego-6134, lego-11458) were likely used in steps where I guessed another type. I did not add them as new pieces, because that would double-count pieces already in the graph. A pass that can edit existing part types should reassign them. I did not change existing parts because this reply may only add pieces and edges.

notes: Page 2 is an introductory page (minifigure opening the box, sorting pieces). It has no building step, so no pieces or joins were added.
Unrelated to this page: the claude.ai Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors need authorization (via claude.ai connector settings) and are unavailable until then.
Page 3 is the first build page. Step 1 puts two blue pins through the 3L connector. Step 2 pushes the pin ends into the two white fairing panels (21 and 22), one on each side.
The connector is drawn dark grey. I assumed lego-42003 in Light Bluish Gray, since the parts list has no black 42003.
The blue pins are drawn as 3L friction pins, so I assumed lego-6558 and not the axle pin lego-43093.
The pins carry no port names for individual ends. Which pin goes into which panel hole is a guess. Both pins pass through the connector and into both panels.
Page 4 builds a small subassembly (steps 1 and 2) and attaches it in step 3 to the page 3 assembly (b1, b4, b5). The axle and pin both go through the 1x5 turquoise beam.
The white round piece on the axle end is drawn as a bush. I assumed lego-62462 White and left its port null. It could be lego-18654 White instead.
The blue pin is assumed to be lego-6558. Which holes of the 1x5 beam the pin and axle use is a guess (pin-hole.1 and pin-hole.2).
Step 3 shows the axle end going into the connector b1 on the page 3 assembly. I assumed it enters the axle hole of b1.
Page 5 builds steps 4 and 5, both done 2x, on the page 3 and 4 assembly.

Step 4: two blue pins, each carrying a short black round piece, go into the free holes of the turquoise beam b10. I assumed the short black round piece is lego-18654 Black. The choice of holes (pin-hole.4 and pin-hole.5) is a guess.

Step 5: a 90° black connector (lego-32014) is pushed into a longer black cylinder, which I took to be lego-62462 Black. The cylinder sits on the blue pin end from step 4. This identification and which port joins which is uncertain, so some port names are null.
Page 6 starts a separate subassembly (steps 6 and 7). The small preview at the top suggests it will later attach to the main model.
Step 6: two black pins go into a black 1x5 beam. Step 7: a dark turquoise 3L perpendicular connector goes onto the pins, with a short black axle in its axle hole.
Hole positions are guesses: the pins go in holes 2 and 4 of the beam, and the axle in step 7 is assumed to be lego-32062.

Page 7, step 8: a second white panel 22 (lego-11947, b24) goes onto the page 6 subassembly (b19 to b23). A black pin (b25) goes into its other hole. I assumed the axle b23 holds the panel at pin-hole.1.
Step 9: the subassembly is turned and joined to the main model. The arrow points at the black round pieces. I assumed the pin b25 goes into b13, which is a guess, so the port is null.
The panel in step 8 is panel 22. The panel in page 3 step 2 was also labelled 22, but this one is a separate piece, since the parts list has 2 of each panel.
Page 8 builds a second copy of the page 6 subassembly (steps 10 and 11), mirroring steps 6 and 7. It is a separate subassembly. The top preview shows it will later fit onto the first one.
Hole positions are guesses, as on page 6. The part in step 11 is lego-42003 Dark Turquoise with a short axle, assumed to be lego-32062, in its axle hole.
Page 9, step 12: panel 21 (lego-11946, b31) goes onto the page 8 subassembly, mirroring page 7 step 8. A black pin (b32) goes into its other hole.
Step 13: the second leg subassembly is joined to the main model. This mirrors page 7 step 9. I assumed the pin b32 goes into b14, which is a guess, so the port is null.
The leg beams b19 and b26 carry the tracks only in a later step, so no track pieces are added here.
Page 10 starts two small separate subassemblies (steps 14 and 15) for the arms. The top preview shows the main body built so far.
Step 14: a black pin goes into a black angled connector. I assumed lego-32014 (90°). A black 32013 or 32192 are also possible.
Step 15: a short black axle goes into a white angled connector. I assumed lego-32015 (112.5°), but the angle is hard to tell from the picture.
Page 11 continues the arm subassembly. The step 14 and 15 pieces already appear joined in step 16, so I added the join b33 (pin) into b36 (pin-hole) here.

Step 16: a dark angled connector goes onto the axle b35, and a blue axle pin goes into its pin hole. I assumed lego-32192 Black for the connector and lego-43093 Blue for the pin. The axle end of the pin then fits the hinge cylinder in step 17.
Step 17: a dark grey hinge plate (lego-44301b) is clipped onto a white hinge cylinder (lego-57360), which sits on the blue axle pin. Which hinge port of 57360 is used is a guess (hinge.1).

Page 12 adds to the arm assembly. Step 18: a round tile goes on the side hole of a 1x1 headlight brick, which sits on the hinge plate b39. I assumed the round tile is lego-98138 Trans-Brown (the picture shows it grey) and the brick is lego-4070 Light Bluish Gray. The picture shows the brick whitish.

Step 19: a white 1x2 brick with studs on two sides (lego-52107) is added, and a black rounded 1x2 plate with two open studs (lego-35480) is pressed on top. The picture is unclear on whether the white brick replaces or sits on the headlight brick. I assumed it sits on b42 and the plate sits on its two top studs.
Only the first stud of the hinge plate b39 and the exact stud positions are guesses.
This page lists parts only, so I did not use the rests_on field. The stacking is recorded as joined edges with studs and anti-studs.

Page 13, step 20: the parts box says 2x lego-60477 White (4x1 slope), but only one is drawn being placed. It goes on the two studs of the black plate b44. I put the second one on the side studs of b43, which is a guess.
The red-box steps 1 and 2 only fold or rotate the hinge between b39 and b40. They add no pieces and no new joins.
Page 14, step 21: no new pieces. The arm subassembly from steps 14 to 20 is attached to the top of the body, where the arrow points at a black round piece with a hole.
I assumed the arm's black angled connector b34 pushes onto the black cylinder b18. Which port and which cylinder it uses is a guess, so the port is null.
Page 15, step 22: a black pin goes into a black angled connector, and the connector goes onto the left shoulder of the body. This mirrors the right arm.
I assumed the connector is lego-32014 Black, like the arm connector b34. Its attachment to the body, the black cylinder b17, is a guess, so the port is null.
Page 16 starts a new subassembly: a launcher unit, shown in the top preview as a turquoise and black part with a vertical clip.

Step 23: a Technic 1x1 brick with pin hole (lego-6541) goes on a black 2x2 corner plate (lego-2420). Step 24: the 1x4 spring shooter (lego-15400) goes on the corner plate beside it. The page has a warning icon about not pointing launchers at faces.
Which stud positions the launcher and the brick use is a guess. The picture only shows the finished layout.

Page 17, step 25: a black corner tile (lego-14719) and a dark turquoise 1x2 grooved tile (lego-3069b) cover the launcher unit. The stud positions are guesses. The corner tile is assumed to sit on b49 studs 1.1 and 1.2. The turquoise tile goes on the free launcher studs 1.3 and 1.4.
Step 26: a white angled connector is mounted on a blue pin that goes into the 1x1 Technic brick b50 pin hole. I assumed lego-32015 White and lego-6558 Blue. The unit is turned over in the step.
Page 18, step 27: no new pieces. The launcher unit from steps 23 to 26 is attached to the robot's left shoulder, on the arrow at b48.
I assumed the pin b47 at the shoulder goes into the axle hole of the white angled connector b54. This is a guess, since the picture does not show the join closely.
Page 19, step 28: a black 3L pin connector with 2 pins (lego-15461) goes onto the blue pin sticking up at the top of the body. Its center hole fits over that pin.
I assumed the blue pin on top is b8, from page 4 step 3.

Page 20 starts a new subassembly (the preview shows a radio-style robot head or body). Step 29: a dark turquoise 1x2 brick goes on a 2x3 plate. Step 30: two Technic 1x1 bricks with pin hole (lego-6541) and two other 1x1 grey bricks go on the plate beside it.
I identified the second grey brick type as lego-4070 (headlight brick). It could be lego-87087 instead.
The exact stud positions of the four 1x1 bricks are guesses: one column on each side of the 1x2 brick.

Page 21 continues the page 20 subassembly (a small radio-like robot head). Step 31: a white 2x2 tile (lego-3068b) goes over the left two columns, and a white 1x2 jumper plate (lego-15573) goes over the right column. Both are assumed from the picture.

Step 32: two black levers with antenna look like lego-298c02 (lever small base with black lever). They go onto the sides of the head. Page 87, step 6: a small side unit is built in the cream box and attached to the model. It has a white 1x2 bracket (lego-99780), a white plate with a stud (assumed lego-15573), a black rounded plate (lego-35480) and a white 1x1 bracket (assumed lego-36840).

The icons are small and hard to read, so the part types and the join ports are guesses. The unit is assumed to attach to the white plate b278 on top of the model. I did not use the lego-15573 jumper port names.

Page 88, step 7: a black L-shaped Technic beam (lego-32526) with two blue axle pins. Step 8: two dark turquoise round pieces (assumed lego-18654 DT) go on the pin ends. This is a separate Technic subassembly, probably an arm.

I assumed the blue pins are lego-43093 (axle pin), because the picture shows them with an axle end and the lego-6558 count is already used up. The pin-hole positions on the L-beam (2 and 6) are guesses. The round pieces have only a pin port in the catalogue, so their end of the join is null.

Page 89, step 9 (2x): two light grey 1x1 Technic bricks with pin hole (lego-6541) go onto the blue pins of the L-beam unit b285. The parts list has only 5 of lego-6541 and I have already used them all. I assumed the type from the icon anyway.
Step 10 has no parts box. The L-beam unit is attached to the body of the small robot. I assumed the two 1x1 bricks clutch the pin-hole plates b279 and b280. Which studs they use is a guess.

Page 90, step 11 (2x): two dark turquoise 1x3 bricks (lego-3622) go on the model, on either side of the black L-beam. Step 12: a white 1x3 plate (lego-3623) and a white 3x3 plate (lego-11212) cover the top.

The pictures give only a rough view, so the stud positions are guesses. The two bricks are joined to the black plates b276 and b277 with null ports. The part counts for lego-11212 and lego-3622 are right at the limits.
Page 91, step 13: two white 1x3 tiles, a white 1x1 plate and another white 1x3 tile cover the top. Step 14 (2x): two light grey pins (lego-3673) go into the pin-hole plates on the sides.

The page shows 2 white 1x3 tiles and a further tile, giving 3 white 1x3 tiles in total. The parts list has only 2 left of lego-63864, so one of the icons may be a different tile type. The stud positions are guesses.
Page 92, step 15: two wheels (lego-13971) with tyres (lego-61254) go onto the grey pins b300 and b301, and a trans-light-blue round tile (assumed lego-98138) goes on the white 1x1 plate b298.
The tyres have no ports in the catalogue, so their joins have null ports.

Page 93, step 16: a light grey 3L axle (lego-4519) goes through the front pin hole of the robot, with a black ball (lego-32474 Technic Ball Joint) on each end. These act as rear or front caster balls.
I assumed the axle goes through the pin hole of b273. The two balls are both joined to the same axle part with the one catalogue port axle.1.

Page 94, step 17: a new small Technic subassembly for the claw arm. A black axle 4 (lego-3705) is pushed into a black perpendicular double-split connector (lego-41678). The top preview shows the arm taking shape. The page also shows a 1:1 drawing of a 4L axle and a 5.5L axle with stop.
The parts list has only 3 black lego-3705 and I have already used 3 on earlier pages. I took the axle type from the picture. The 5.5 axle drawn in the 1:1 box is not used in this step.

Page 95, step 18: a dark grey 5.5L axle with stop (lego-59426) is put through the connector b311, and a light grey bush (lego-32123b) goes on the end of axle b310. Step 19: a black 90° angled connector (assumed lego-32014) goes onto the other end of the long axle, and a short black axle (lego-32062) goes into its other hole.
The parts list has only 4 black lego-32014 and all 4 are used earlier. This is a 5th use from the picture. The axle holes and pin holes are guesses.
Page 96, step 20: another black 90° angled connector (lego-32014, b317) goes on the end of the arm, with a short black axle (lego-32062, b316) in its other hole. This builds a long zig-zag claw arm.
The pieces are not in stock by the parts list (lego-32014 over the limit). I assumed the types from the picture. The port choices (axle-hole.1 and pin-hole.1) are guesses.
Page 97, step 21: a white angled connector goes on the end of the arm, and a light grey 3L axle (lego-4519) goes into its other hole. This builds the claw arm's wrist.
I assumed lego-32013 White, since the other white angled types are used up. The icon could also be lego-32015 or lego-32192. The port choices are guesses.

Page 98, step 22 (2x): two white round cylinders (assumed lego-62462 White) each get a black pin at both ends. One end of each cylinder plugs into the arm's bend: one into b315 and one into b317. The page shows 4 black pins and 2 white cylinders in the parts box.

The parts list has only 2 white lego-62462 and one is used earlier. I used the catalogue ports pin.1 and pin.2 for the cylinder ends. The join to b315 and b317 is a guess and could clash with the pins already there.
Page 99, step 23: the claw arm built on pages 94 to 98 is attached to the robot body. A light grey bush (lego-32123b) goes on the axle end that sticks out of the body, to hold the arm in place.

The axle b310 is assumed to run through the black L-beam b285, at pin-hole.4. The two white cylinders are said to plug into the body's side pins, but I could not tell where, so I did not add those joins.

Page 100, step 24: a second arm is started, which is the mirror of the first. A dark grey 5.5L axle with stop (lego-59426) goes into a black connector, assumed lego-41678 again. The parts list has only 1 of lego-41678 and it is used on page 94, so the icon may be lego-32039 instead.
The axle port on the connector is a guess.
Page 101, steps 25 and 26: the second arm repeats the first arm's steps 19 and 20. Each step adds a short black axle (lego-32062) and a black 90° angled connector (lego-32014).
The lego-32014 count is over the parts list again, as on earlier pages. I assumed the types from the icons. The ports are guesses.

Page 102, step 27: this mirrors step 21 on the first arm. A white angled connector (lego-32013, assumed again) goes on the end of the second arm, and a light grey 3L axle (lego-4519) goes into its other hole.
The port choices are guesses.
Page 103, step 28: no new pieces. The second arm from pages 100 to 102 is attached to the robot body. The arrow points at the free axle end at the back of the model.
I assumed the second arm's connector b321 sits on the axle b310 that sticks out of the body. This is a guess about how the two arms share the axle.

Page 104, step 29: a red Zamor sphere (lego-54821) is held between the two claw arms. It is not fastened to anything, so I recorded it as touching the two claw axles b318 and b327. The page has a warning icon about not throwing parts at faces.
